owner_decision: On 2026-11-22 the owner asked for the valve, seat and guide gap to be filled from published data under declared assumptions. Review: Wolfe Classics, the seller of the scanned head; nobody has been contacted.
rule: Every value below is a published value of another head, a range from the maker's catalogue, a fit on the scan, or an explicitly assumed value. Each carries its source id or its hypothesis id. None is a measurement of the specimen. Published values are hypothesis H16; the inlet and exhaust roles are hypothesis H09.
frame: stations s along each valve's datum axis (params/feature-fits.json, group_datums), positive toward the cam side; radii r from that axis

head_diameter_mm.how: the only intake diameter common to both catalogue families that a 935 head of 2.85 to 3.3 litres could belong to (45-49 and 49-53 mm), and the production 930 Turbo value

stem_diameter_mm.how: the maker lists 8 mm stems for every family; the production 9 mm stem does not enter the fitted guide bore of 8.51 mm

overall_length_mm.how: length of a published 8 mm-stem inlet valve for the 911 two-valve head (52 mm head); the production 9 mm valve is 110.1 mm

seat_contact_width_mm.how: 911 3.0 and 3.2 inlet seat width, measured on the 45 degree surface

contact_inset_from_face_edge_mm.how: read as the slant distance from the outer edge of the valve's 45 degree face to the contact line; the page's wording ('the top of the edge of the 45 angle') admits another reading
quotes: We want this line to be about .5mm from the top of the edge of the 45 angle

margin_thickness_mm.how: explicit assumption, no source; the value of the assembly screen (params/assembly-case.json, H10)

face_radial_width_mm.how: explicit assumption, no source; the value of the assembly screen

tulip_length_mm.how: explicit assumption, no source; a straight cone from the face to the stem, as in the assembly screen

largest_lift_mm.how: the production 930 Turbo 3.0 inlet lift; no lift of a 934, 935 or Xtreme cam was found

head_diameter_mm.how: the only exhaust diameter common to both catalogue families (38-41.5 and 41.5-42.5 mm), and the production 930 Turbo value

overall_length_mm.how: length of a published 8 mm-stem exhaust valve for the 911 two-valve head (44 mm head); the production 9 mm valve is 108.4 mm

quotes: We want this line to be about .5mm from the top of the edge of the 45 angle

angles_deg.how: 911 2.0 to 3.2 seat angles, each measured from the valve's plane: cone half-angles from the axis of 60, 45 and 15 degrees

placement.value: the 45 degree seat cone passes through the mid-band circle of the fitted seat (params/feature-fits.json, about the datum axis); the closed valve's contact band lies on it

quotes: Hardened ductile iron intake and exhaust valve seats

inner_diameter.value: the fitted throat diameter of each valve
inner_diameter.how: the insert bore is taken as the fitted throat (confirmed on held-out vertices for both valves, params/feature-confirmation.json)

valve_y_plus.how: the 930 Turbo exhaust seat ring is listed as 46 mm without saying which dimension; read as the outside diameter because a 41.5 mm valve must seal inside it

valve_y_minus.how: no inlet figure was found; the exhaust ring's outside diameter less its valve (46 - 41.5 = 4.5 mm) added to the inlet valve: a derived assumption

height_mm.how: explicit assumption, no source: no published height of a 911 or 930 seat ring was found

chamber_face.value: flush with the combustion face of the closed valve

interference_mm.blocker: no published interference of a 911 or 930 seat ring was found; not needed by any body

outside_diameter.value: fitted valve_y_minus_guide_od_cam (12.87 mm about the datum axis)
outside_diameter.how: the scan shows the guide where it stands out of the spring pocket; the published 911 guide is 13.06 mm

port_end.value: the fitted cone valve_y_minus_guide_od_port (11.99 mm at mid-band, half-angle 5.85 degrees about the datum axis) from the guide tip until it reaches the outside diameter

stations.value: from the start of the guide-bore window to its end: the bore is acquired at both ends (valve_y_minus_guide_bore)

outside_diameter.value: fitted valve_y_plus_guide_od_cam (13.02 mm about the datum axis)

port_end.value: straight: the fitted port-end boss valve_y_plus_guide_boss_port is a cylinder of 13.04 mm

stations.value: from the start of the port-end boss window to the end of the cam-end outside-diameter window; the middle is not acquired

inside_diameter_mm.how: the 8 mm stem plus a running clearance of 0.05 mm, an explicit assumption; the published wear limits of the 9 mm production guide (9.10 and 9.13 mm) bound the clearance at 0.10 to 0.13 mm. The fitted guide bore of 8.51 mm is not used: it would leave 0.51 mm of clearance

press_fit_mm.how: 911 guide press fit in a reamed boss bore; not modelled in the head body, which keeps the scanned guides

quotes: a tubular section of brass, bronze, or silicon bronze, called a valve guide

not_modelled: valve springs, retainers, keepers and rockers
the head bores the guides and seats are pressed into: the v2 body keeps the scanned guides and seats as one solid
fillets of the valve head and the throat blends
the concave underside of a real valve head: the tulip here is a straight solid cone, so the valves' volumes (18.6 and 14.5 cm3) overstate any real valve and give no mass
the oil cooling of an exhaust guide or seat that some 935 heads are described with
